en: The Legend of the Elder Sucintita Sudhāvagga, Number Two I was once a brahmin youth named Sucintita, living in the city of Benares. Having heard that the Buddha had appeared in the world, I went to the presence of the Teacher. There, seated upon a seat of kusa grass, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One, was teaching the Dhamma to the assembly. Seeing the Teacher, the World-Honored One, I approached him and paid homage at his feet. Then, sitting to one side, I addressed the Blessed One with these verses: “O Sage, you who have reached the further shore of all phenomena, You who have crossed over the flood and reached the dry land, You who have transcended birth and death and attained Nibbāna— To you, the Fully Enlightened One, I pay homage. Having thus praised the Teacher, I took up a handful of flowers and scattered them over the head of the Blessed One. Then, having made this offering, I stood before the Teacher and spoke these words: “May I, through this root of merit, In a future life, attain the state of Buddhahood. May I become a teacher for the world, Just as you are now, O Great Sage. The Teacher, knowing my aspiration, spoke these words to me: “You shall indeed become a Buddha in the future; Your name shall be Padumuttara, And you shall bring great benefit to the world. Having received this prophecy from the Teacher, I departed from his presence. For eighty-four thousand years, I practiced the ten wholesome paths of action. When the time came for me to pass away, I was reborn in the realm of the Thirty-three gods. After passing away from there, I was reborn among humans. Throughout many hundreds of thousands of existences, I never fell into the lower realms. In every birth, I possessed great wisdom and was endowed with the five supernormal powers. In my final existence, I was born into a wealthy family in the city of Sāvatthī. When I grew up, I left the household life and went forth under the guidance of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One, Kassapa. Having gone forth, I applied myself to meditation and attained the four jhānas. Through the power of my previous vows, I was able to recollect my past lives. Having seen my own former deeds, I developed a mind of renunciation and, with a heart free from attachment, I passed away to be reborn in the Brahma-world. There, I dwelt for an aeon, enjoying the bliss of the Brahmās. When that aeon ended, I descended from the Brahma-world and was reborn in the human realm. In this present age, I have met the Buddha Gotama, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One. Having gone forth under his guidance, I have realized the fruit of Arhatship. Thus, by the power of my former resolve and the merit of my offerings, I have attained the supreme state of peace. May all beings likewise cultivate such wholesome roots and reach the end of suffering. This is the legend of the Elder Sucintita, the second in the Sudhāvagga.
“To Tissa, the Protector of the World,
I gave a pure seat;
joyful, with a joyful heart.”
Of the Buddha, the Kinsman of the Sun.
Eighteen aeons ago from now,
I was a king named Mahāruci.
There was abundant enjoyment and no small amount of bedding;
having given a seat to the Buddha, [one obtains such rewards].
With a serene mind,
I experience my own karma,
well-performed by myself in the past.
In the ninety-two aeons since then,
because I gave that seat,
I have never known a state of misery.
This is the fruit of giving a seat.
In the thirty-eighth aeon from now,
you three will be universal monarchs (cakkavattins).
Ruci, Uparuci,
and Mahāruci as the third;
the four analytical knowledges (paṭisambhidā).
the Buddha's teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the Venerable Thera Sucintika speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Sucintika is the second.
